section_plan.title: Objective
content_bullets: Deep learning (DL) techniques perform well on computer vision and language tasks but gaps exist in applying DL to physics problems
Propose foundational research to enable neural networks (NNs) to perform well on physics tasks across broad spectrum of physical environments and boundary conditions
Develop new methods attaining high accuracy in large problem spaces characteristic of physical domains
Demonstrate utility on three Navy-relevant physics tasks: underwater acoustics, electromagnetic propagation, structural health monitoring
notebook_topics: Navy applications: acoustics, EM propagation, structural health monitoring
citation_hints: Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (Chen et al.)

section_plan.title: Background and Related Work
content_bullets: Trained NNs generalize well on CV and language tasks (medical diagnosis, self-driving vehicles, Navy applications)
Recent integration of NNs into physics emulators: UDE, PINN, NODE
Benefits: orders of magnitude speedups, lower implementation costs, ability to shape PDEs to conform with observations
Merger of scientific computing, simulation, and neural networks described as 'Simulation Intelligence'
Gap: NNs do not generalize well enough for universal physics solutions across all environments and boundary conditions
Literature lacks evidence of NN solutions providing good test performance over entire range of physically realizable inputs
No prior studies on generalization in physics domains
notebook_topics: generalization in computer vision vs physics
citation_hints: Physics meets ML survey (Meng et al. 2022)
Generalization studies (Chatterjee & Zielinski 2022, Dziugaite et al. 2020, Jiang et al. 2019, 2020)

section_plan.title: Problem Formulation
content_bullets: Research Hypothesis 1: Properties and methods improving generalization in mature DL (CV, NLP) will also improve generalization on physics tasks
Research Hypothesis 2: Physics equations, symmetry, and invariances can be used to improve generalization in each domain
Technical Challenge 1: Identify generalization techniques from mature DL methods that work across physics tasks
Technical Challenge 2: Derive generalization methods for three physics domain testbeds using physics equations
Large-scale investigation of generalization in Navy DL physics applications using NRL-exclusive data
Focus on three domains: underwater acoustics (transmission loss), RF propagation (atmospheric), structural health monitoring
citation_hints: Data augmentation in NMT (Li et al. 2019)

section_plan.title: Approach
content_bullets: Task 1: Create baselines for three domains using existing implementations
Acoustics baseline: PALIS project neural network methods for transmission loss estimation
Meteorology baseline: Modify PALIS for COAMPS NWP data and RF propagation
Structural health monitoring baseline: MINC project real-time NN system for material damage
Task 2: Investigate NN generalization in physics domains - study properties from mature DL applications
Properties investigated: data, data augmentation, data diversity, architecture, activation functions, hyperparameters
Define generalization measures: complexity, norm, sharpness measures
Investigate transfer learning and unsupervised pretraining mechanisms
Task 3: Improve generalization using physics equations, symmetries, invariances
Develop novel data augmentation methods respecting physics constraints (cutout, patch masking)
Utilize Neural Architecture Search and Hyperparameter Optimization
Develop dynamic activation functions using cyclical training
Novel contrastive output augmentation loss function
citation_hints: Lifted structure embedding (Oh Song et al. 2016)

section_plan.title: Methodology
content_bullets: Acoustics domain: Train NNs for 2D TL maps across time, broad spectrum of ocean properties (temperature, salinity, sound speed), source depths, receiver locations, frequencies
Meteorology domain: Develop RF propagation maps across location, time, atmospheric properties (humidity, temperature, pressure), trapping conditions, RF source heights/frequencies
Structural health monitoring: Enable systems to perform across variety of metallic surfaces, sensor configurations, complex geometries, non-linear wave dynamics, damage characteristics
Evaluation approach: Define experiments to measure generalization ability along dimensions of importance
Example experiment: Test sensitivity to small changes in source frequency and location
Subject matter expert evaluation of promising methods
Deliverables: Methods improving generalization across domains, methodology for designing domain-specific methods, updated implementations

section_plan.title: Results
content_bullets: FY24 results: Identified that standard CV generalization techniques (mixup, SAM) prove ineffective for physics applications
Necessitated development of domain-specific methodologies incorporating fundamental physical principles
FY25 progress: Neural operators (NSNO) for Helmholtz equations show 60% error reduction vs standard FNO
NSNO demonstrates improved stability for large wavenumbers
CLIP pretraining experiments: Expected benefits not realized, pretrained models generally inferior to local training
Approximate solution methods: Ray-trace vectors as secondary input perform equivalently to low-resolution TL with reduced runtime
Cyclical generation experiments: Method could not effectively evaluate generated TL quality
Mixup experiments across frequency ranges: Results vary by domain, generally small improvements in test metrics with degraded training metrics
SAM optimizer experiments: Increased training time without clear performance benefits
Frequency-specific training: Training on subset of frequencies shows degraded performance on held-out frequencies

section_plan.title: Discussion
content_bullets: Neural operators represent significant advancement for physics-guided neural networks
NSNO architecture mimics analytical Neumann series expansion, providing mathematical grounding
Multi-scale skip connections crucial for capturing broad wavelength ranges in high-frequency solutions
CLIP pretraining limitations: Universal applicability not achieved, benefits diminish with decreasing training dataset sizes
Physics-specific constraints limit applicability of standard CV data augmentation techniques
Importance of domain expertise: Understanding physics equations, symmetries, invariances essential for effective model design
Computational efficiency gains: Neural operators provide substantial speedup while maintaining accuracy for sensitive tasks
Generalization-accuracy tradeoff: Methods improving test generalization often degrade training performance
Domain-specific approaches necessary: Single universal method insufficient across all physics domains

section_plan.title: Summary and Conclusions
content_bullets: Demonstrated that standard DL generalization techniques require significant adaptation for physics domains
Neural operators (particularly NSNO) show promise for solving heterogeneous Helmholtz equations with improved generalization
CLIP pretraining approach did not provide expected benefits for physics domain foundation models
Physics-informed constraints and domain-specific methods essential for achieving robust generalization
Established baselines and evaluation frameworks for three Navy-relevant physics domains
Identified key differences between CV/NLP generalization and physics domain generalization
Future work: Further development of neural operator frameworks, investigation of physics-specific data augmentation, exploration of hybrid physics-ML approaches
Transition potential: Methods developed have high potential to improve existing Navy applications (PALIS, COAMPS, MINC)

section_plan.title: Transitions
content_bullets: PALIS project: Neural network methods for transmission loss estimation transitioning to tactical decision aids (TDAs)
Potential to replace expensive NSPE algorithms in submarine sonar systems
COAMPS integration: RF propagation neural surrogates for meteorology applications
MINC project: Real-time structural health monitoring systems for naval platforms
Transition to Builder software for platform maintenance scheduling
Enhanced sonar prediction accuracy improving ASW effectiveness
Real-time EM propagation models supporting counter-EW tactics
Reduced computational requirements enabling shipboard deployment
Improved operational capabilities through faster simulation and prediction
